uncovered_scopes: Complete invariant and transition inventory of all three normative roadmaps
Compiler, planner, manifest, CLI and editor invariants
Production installer and migration executors, bootstrap and control-format upgrades
Typed row-function semantics, persisted-proof ABI boundaries and Same
Versioned queue payload transformations, quarantine replay and external effects
Staged uniqueness, offline changes, catch-up and pruning

invariants.INV-ABI: A migration's processing ABI cannot change after any batch, provisional work or committed target-generation application write; reprocessing uses a later version and fresh generation.
invariants.INV-ADDITIVE-READ: Independently compiled old and new applications read the same logical rows across additive schema versions.
invariants.INV-ADDITIVE-WRITE: An additive old-version write preserves columns owned by newer versions.
invariants.INV-ATOMIC-WRITE: Competing application writes observe transaction boundaries and never publish a partial update.
invariants.INV-ATTEMPT: Only the exact current live queue attempt may renew or publish an outcome; expired and dead claims are not silently revived.
invariants.INV-BOOT-LOCK: Only the backend holding the non-expiring session boot lock performs install work; an expired observability lease cannot release that lock.
invariants.INV-CATALOG-DEFAULT: An extra column default is benign only when its supported scalar type and recognized constant cannot execute code or reject an omitted-column insert; arbitrary casts, domains and computations are drift.
invariants.INV-CATALOG-EVIDENCE: Catalog evidence includes behavior-affecting relation, column, constraint, index, trigger and policy properties; isolated property changes are distinguishable without catalog-row OIDs or raw DDL text.
invariants.INV-CATALOG-EXPRESSION: Catalog expressions use one server deparser under an empty search path, with matching types and collations; comparison objects and settings do not survive the probe transaction.
invariants.INV-CATALOG-EXTRA-INDEX: Nonunique indexes are not automatically harmless: expressions, predicates and plain-key width limits can reject old-valid writes; extra indexes require classification and an old-key domain proof.
invariants.INV-CLAIMANT: Retirement waits for retiring claimants only; surviving claimants retain their attempt, status and lease when restamped.
invariants.INV-CLOCK: Explicit model time is monotone and bounded arithmetic cannot wrap a lease into validity.
invariants.INV-CONTRACT: Physical contract follows retirement and the compatibility switch, and an interrupted contract remains resumable.
invariants.INV-DDL-JOB: An index statement and its final catalog verification hold the same backend's shared job lock and admitted version fence.
invariants.INV-DDL-TERMINAL: Contract drains shared job locks and records terminal with its immutable removal version before destructive DDL; DROP waits for that version's compatibility switch, and a stale worker cannot resurrect the job.
invariants.INV-DECODER: Queue claims remain inside the admitted decoder window and never claim a future payload version.
invariants.INV-EXPAND: Retirement's coordinator lock excludes a competing expansion.
invariants.INV-FENCE: Every excluded writer is drained before retirement and cannot resume writing after its version is retired.
invariants.INV-FINAL: Retirement commits only after every affected row is accepted at its target generation; accepted batches survive coordinator abort.
invariants.INV-FLOOR: Admission and compatibility floors are ordered, monotone and consistent with committed lifecycle evidence.
invariants.INV-GENERATION: Row generations advance one step at a time within the permanent smallint generation bound.
invariants.INV-HARNESS: Interleavings identify actor and occurrence, reject ambiguous control input, and fail with bounded waits and useful state dumps.
invariants.INV-HISTORY: Version identities and classifications are immutable, consecutive and complete; an equal retry remains transaction-safe.
invariants.INV-INDEX-BUILD: The model distinguishes absent, active-invalid, abandoned-invalid and valid index catalog states.
invariants.INV-INDEX-IDENTITY: An index job retains its declared semantic identity; a same-named different catalog object is not adopted.
invariants.INV-INDEX-READY: Index readiness requires the exact expected valid catalog object, not a worker's recorded intention.
invariants.INV-INDEX-RECOVERY: Recovery drops only an inactive invalid remnant and preserves an active or successfully completed build.
invariants.INV-INSTALL-ATOMIC: Initial expansion publishes its lifecycle and admission singleton atomically; a database born at V9 never invents V8 history.
invariants.INV-INSTALL-CATALOG: Initial install and additive expansion verify the selected catalog before recording expansion and preserve completed objects across recovery.
invariants.INV-INSTALL-TARGET: The first lock holder persists an immutable initial target; a newer successor completes that target before expanding further.
invariants.INV-JSONB-COMPATIBILITY: A new JSONB fallback decoder accepting old data does not imply that admitted old readers can decode new writes; compiled readers and writers are checked in both directions.
invariants.INV-JSONB-RETENTION: Reads and later deployments leave untouched legacy JSONB representations intact; removing their decoder requires rewrite evidence after incompatible old writers are excluded.
invariants.INV-LEASE: Scheduling lease tokens increase on takeover and stale executors cannot publish another holder's work.
invariants.INV-LIFECYCLE: Only validated lifecycle edges append history and committed history agrees with the admission singleton.
invariants.INV-MATRIX: A PostgreSQL matrix lane checks the connected server's actual major before constructing fixtures.
invariants.INV-PRIVILEGE: Application and worker roles cannot bypass lifecycle guards by writing control tables or shadowing control functions.
invariants.INV-QUARANTINE: Quarantine records a current rejection after coordinator abort; changed, accepted or deleted rows cannot retain stale evidence.
invariants.INV-QUEUE-FLOOR: At floor commit no non-quarantined durable job remains below the new floor.
invariants.INV-READ: A strict read buffers its query result and delivers only after successful admission and transaction commit, retaining table locks until then.
invariants.INV-REGISTRY-ALLOCATION: Concurrent schema families allocate distinct bounded fence namespaces and UUIDs; aborted or exhausted allocations never replace a committed identity or use a reserved key.
invariants.INV-REGISTRY-OWNER: The global fence registry and its identity sequence have the trusted NOLOGIN control owner and no non-owner mutation grants.
invariants.INV-REGISTRY-SHAPE: A pre-existing registry matches the independent permanent-table, constraint, index and sequence catalog; lookalikes, inheritance, rewrite rules and altered definitions are refused without aborting caller work.
invariants.INV-REPAIR-EXECUTOR: Serving repair chains may be compatible prefixes, but the final-pass executor carries every recorded amendment.
invariants.INV-REPAIR-HISTORY: Repair chains are positive, bounded, gap-free and append-only without changing the migration's own identity.
invariants.INV-REPAIR-ORDER: Recorded repairs run in sequence on a rejected row and stop at the first acceptance.
invariants.INV-REPAIR-SCOPE: Repairs cannot reinterpret rows already accepted by the frozen transform or apply a stale row evaluation.
invariants.INV-ROW-REVISION: The oracle distinguishes row revisions and refuses stale evaluations and revision overflow.
invariants.INV-SQL-CLASS: Every normative-roadmap SQL fence explicitly declares whether it is executable, illustrative or a generated snapshot.
invariants.INV-SQL-SOURCE: The documented bootstrap transaction and contract recipe are generated from the exact fixtures executed by the PostgreSQL tests.
invariants.INV-TOPOLOGY: A lagged replica's local floor and catalog cannot authorize a strict application read across primary retirement.
invariants.INV-TRACEABILITY: Every registered harness invariant and transition has a named test, every test names an invariant, and every model operation is inventoried.
invariants.INV-UNIQUE-WINDOW: A failed ready-but-invalid unique index may already reject old-version writes; readiness and cleanup must use actual PostgreSQL catalog states.
invariants.INV-VERSION: Schema versions are positive signed integers and cannot allocate the reserved boot-fence key.
invariants.INV-WINDOW: A transforming expansion closes an additive epoch and respects the bounded compatibility window.

TR-ABI-BATCH.statement: Commit a batch or provisional pass with its processing ABI.

TR-ABI-SELECT.statement: Select an execution ABI before processing is locked.

TR-ABI-WRITE.statement: Commit a target-generation application value and its ABI evidence under the same admitted writer fence, independently of backfill counters.

TR-ADMIT.statement: Check the reader's version against the current admission floor.

TR-BACKFILL.statement: Commit an accepted row at its next generation.

TR-BOOT-CRASH.statement: Lose the boot backend and its lock while retaining committed install work.

TR-BOOT-EXPAND.statement: Record a verified additive successor after completing the initial target.

TR-BOOT-LOCK.statement: Acquire the non-expiring backend boot lock.

TR-BOOT-RELEASE.statement: Release the backend's boot lock after verified install work.

TR-CATALOG-COMPARE.statement: Compare catalog expressions in temporary matching column contexts and classify extra-column defaults without evaluating computing expressions.

TR-CLAIM.statement: Claim a pending or expired processing job with a fresh attempt.

TR-COMPLETE.statement: Complete the exact live queue attempt.

TR-CONTRACT.statement: Record contract intent, switch compatibility, and finish physical work.

TR-CRASH.statement: Lose volatile locks and sessions while retaining committed work.

TR-DEAD.statement: Move the exact live queue attempt to the dead letter.

TR-ENQUEUE.statement: Enqueue a payload stamped with the admitted writer version.

TR-EXPAND.statement: Record the next immutable expansion or safely retry the current one.

TR-EXPIRY.statement: Advance explicit time through lease expiry.

TR-INDEX-BACKEND-DEATH.statement: Lose an index backend's locks and active statement.

TR-INDEX-CLEANUP.statement: Remove an inactive invalid remnant before rebuilding.

TR-INDEX-DROP.statement: Drop a terminal job's physical index idempotently after the removing contract version's compatibility switch.

TR-INDEX-ENTER.statement: Acquire the shared DDL-job lock and recheck current ownership.

TR-INDEX-EXIT.statement: Release the shared job lock after statement completion and verification.

TR-INDEX-FAILURE.statement: An active concurrent build fails and leaves an invalid remnant.

TR-INDEX-PLAN.statement: Register an immutable index job identity.

TR-INDEX-START.statement: Start a concurrent build with the current scheduling token.

TR-INDEX-SUCCESS.statement: The server completes a concurrent build, independently of lease expiry.

TR-INDEX-TERMINAL.statement: Contract records terminal and its immutable removal version after all shared job holders drain.

TR-INDEX-VERIFY.statement: Verify the actual catalog before publishing readiness.

TR-INSTALL-OBJECT.statement: Commit or verify one selected catalog object in a short transaction.

TR-INSTALL-RECORD.statement: Atomically record complete initial history and admission, including equal retries.

TR-INSTALL-SELECT.statement: Persist or observe the initial install target under the boot lock.

TR-INVALIDATE.statement: An old writer invalidates derived generation and rejection evidence.

TR-LEASE.statement: Acquire a scheduling lease or validate its current commit token.

TR-MATRIX-CONNECT.statement: Verify the actual server major for the selected matrix lane.

TR-QUARANTINE-REFRESH.statement: Re-read a rejected key after abort and update or clear quarantine.

TR-READ.statement: Execute and buffer a query before admission and delivery.

TR-REJECT.statement: The frozen transform rejects a row below its target generation.

TR-REGISTRY-ALLOCATE.statement: Allocate a unique namespace and logical database UUID under the database-wide bootstrap lock, preserving committed identities across failures.

TR-REGISTRY-VERIFY.statement: Verify registry ownership, exact catalog shape, identity sequence and non-owner grants in a rollback-only comparison savepoint.

TR-RENEW.statement: Renew the exact live queue attempt under version admission.

TR-REPAIR.statement: Validate the public repair lifecycle edge independently of ordinary expansion.

TR-REPAIR-ADMIT.statement: Accept compatible repair prefixes for ordinary serving.

TR-REPAIR-FINAL.statement: Require the complete recorded repair chain for final-pass execution.

TR-REPAIR-RECORD.statement: Append or idempotently retry an immutable repair identity.

TR-REPAIR-ROW.statement: Apply the next recorded repair only to a current rejected row.

TR-REPLAY.statement: Pause and resume physical WAL replay on an owned standby.

TR-RESTAMP.statement: Restamp old jobs before floor commit while preserving surviving claims.

TR-RETIRE.statement: Drain retiring fences and atomically commit the floor after final passes.

TR-RETRY.statement: Requeue the exact live attempt with its surviving schema stamp.

TR-ROW-ADD.statement: Register a source row owing one bounded generation step.

TR-ROW-DELETE.statement: An admitted application deletes a row and its stale rejection evidence.

TR-SCHEDULE.statement: Register, pause, observe and release a named deterministic boundary.

TR-SQL-CLASSIFY.statement: Classify each complete normative-roadmap SQL fence before execution.

TR-SQL-DOCUMENT.statement: Render the executed control bootstrap fixture into the normative document without changing surrounding text.

TR-TRACEABILITY-CHECK.statement: Validate source metadata and regenerate the deterministic coverage map.

TR-WRITE.statement: Begin an admitted fenced writer and release it at transaction end.
